title: Structural basis for loading of transcription repair-coupling factor Mfd onto stalled elongation complexes.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded both deposited atomic models from the Protein Data Bank (PDB): 9N07 (7.57 MB mmCIF, 71,200 atom lines, ligands ADP + BEF (beryllium trifluoride) + Mg + 2 Zn) and 9N11 (7.51 MB mmCIF, 70,698 atom lines, Mg + 2 Zn only). HEAD-checked both cryo-electron microscopy density maps (EMD-48776, 7.5 MB gzipped; EMD-48802, 9.9 MB gzipped). Unzipped the full Europe PMC supplement: one 3.2 MB Word file containing three supplemental figures plus one cryo-EM statistics table, and four figure images. No tabular data file of any kind exists.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Particle counts (2,788,386 and 212,950 initial images; 96,588 and 13,808 final particles) and resolutions (3.5 A and 4.3 A) come from Supplementary Table 1, which I read. The gel-shift displacement assay results are images in figures only; no quantified measurements are tabulated anywhere.

a1_downloadable.note: Both PDB models and both EMDB maps download freely with no login; I fetched both mmCIF files (7.5 MB each) successfully.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: There is no table and therefore no label column anywhere. The deposited data are two atomic coordinate files and two three-dimensional density maps; any prediction target (e.g. a conformational-state class or a domain rotation angle) would have to be constructed from scratch by the modeller.

a3_inputs_present.note: Protein sequences and atomic coordinates are present inside the mmCIF files, so inputs would not need external lookup.

a4_units_stated.note: Coordinates are in Angstroms and B-factors in Angstrom squared, as standard for PDB/EMDB depositions; the cryo-EM statistics table states all its units.

a5_enough_rows.note: The whole dataset is 2 structures (one new intermediate L1 plus one newly identified L1.5), each one example of one complex from one organism. The checklist needs about 1,500 labelled rows, or 400 for classification. Two is three orders of magnitude short. Counting atoms (about 71,000 each) is not counting examples: every atom belongs to the same single complex.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~33 MB total (two mmCIF files plus two gzipped maps)
a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially laptop-sized; this is the one thing the dataset has going for it.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Supplementary Table 1 claims 71,263 and 70,701 non-hydrogen atoms; I counted 71,200 and 70,698 atom records in the downloaded files, agreeing to within rounding of hydrogens/alternates.

a8_label_provenance.note: The structures themselves are model-fitted interpretations of density maps, and the only derived quantity in the supplement (a modelled UvrA2B placement, root-mean-square deviation 1.3 A over 72 atoms) is the output of a superposition done in PyMOL, i.e. a computational model's output rather than an independent physical measurement. There is no measured outcome variable to predict.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (a protein language model) or Boltz/AlphaFold-style structure predictors

integration.partner_dataset: Protein Data Bank plus EMDB (the public archives of experimental structures and cryo-electron microscopy maps)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written usefully: joining two structures to the PDB gives you the PDB, and this paper contributes two entries to an archive that already holds hundreds of thousands, so the combination answers no question the archive does not already answer.

controls.positive_control: None available: with two examples there is nothing to hold out, so no control can distinguish a working pipeline from a broken one.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is meaningless on two items.
controls.external_validation: The authors' own earlier seven-structure series (including 6X26 and 6X50, used here as starting models) is the nearest thing, but nine structures total is still far too few.

honest_claim_h3: No honest model claim is possible from this paper's data: with two deposited structures of a single protein-protein-DNA complex from one organism, any trained model would be describing two data points.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the shape of a stalled transcription machine to predict which step of the repair-factor loading pathway it is in.
plain_idea.train_on: What the model would see: the three-dimensional coordinates (or the density map) of an Mfd-RNA-polymerase complex. The number of examples this paper provides is 2 (verified by downloading both deposited structures).
plain_idea.predict: Which stage of the loading pathway the complex occupies (the authors' labels L1, L1.5, L2, C1-C5). The true answer comes from the authors' own expert interpretation of cryo-electron microscopy density, not from an independent measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: In principle, structural biologists who sort millions of cryo-EM particle images by conformation would value an automatic state classifier; in practice this paper supplies two examples, so nothing could be learned here and the project is not viable on this data.

ml_idea: The only conceivable task is classifying the conformational stage of an Mfd-elongation-complex intermediate from its structure or density map, which would need thousands of labelled states; this paper adds two. The raw particle images that could in principle support a cryo-EM heterogeneity model (2.79 million and 213 thousand images) were not deposited to EMPIAR, and raw cryo-EM data is excluded by our own size and raw-data rules anyway.

effort.compute_note: No compute estimate is meaningful because no feature/label table can be built; the 33 MB working set is the measured total of the four deposited files.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the deposited structures. It is 2 (PDB 9N07 and 9N11, EMD-48776 and EMD-48802), and that one count kills the project in under a minute.

verdict_reason: Fails A5 outright: the entire dataset is two cryo-electron microscopy structures of one complex, roughly 1,500-fold short of the minimum labelled rows. Also fails A2 (no table and no label column exists) and A8 (the only derived number is a PyMOL superposition, not a measurement). This is a high-quality mechanistic structural biology paper that simply produces no machine-learning dataset; I verified this by downloading both structures and unzipping the entire supplement, which contains only figures and a cryo-EM statistics table.
